newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Mixed after Fed move.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Mixed after Fed move.

text.p: Australian bond yield spreads were mixed against the dollar bloc in the aftermath of Tuesday's 25 basis point tightening in U.S. interest rates which followed the Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread see-sawed around Tuesday's local closing levels as the market began to speculate about the possibility of a further U.S. rate hikes in the coming months.
Speculation on further tightenings are expected to weigh on the U.S. Treasury market, and are likely to put pressure on the Australian market.
"However, there is no need for the US-Australia differential to blow out further from the current 130 basis points," economists at ANZ securities said in a report.
"Indeed, there is a reasonable case, given low growth, low inflation and further fiscal contraction to come in the budget, for some narrowing in this differential," the report added.
Canadian bonds ended Tuesday little change on the Fed move, while New Zealand debt took the news negatively and was outperformed by the whole bloc.
